spots.name: Red Barn Pool (Klaskanine forested section)
spots.blurb: Forested deep pool visible in spinthehandle YouTube shorts video, features red barn structure on adjacent property and deep green water below dense forest canopy. Appears to be a private section but visible from nearby access.
spots.access_note: Estimated from satellite imagery at the bend ~1.5mi upriver from Sigfredson County Park where red barn structure is visible. Appears to be private land; permission likely needed.

spots.name: Wilson River Lower Section (Guide Service Pool)
spots.blurb: Steelhead fishing location documented by Lewis and Clark Guide Service in 2016 where bobber dogging technique was used. Known guide service location.
spots.access_note: Access via Lewis and Clark Guide Service boat ramp; private guide service operations. Bobber dogging (bobber and jig drift) technique recommended.

spots.name: North Fork Nehalem - Fish Hatchery to Aldervale Section
spots.blurb: Jet boat accessible section from the fish hatchery down to Aldervale. Video title mentions '35 inch' fish caught. Described as hatchery-to-Aldervale run.
spots.access_note: Boat access from fish hatchery; appears to be a guide area. Estimated coords at midpoint of hatchery to Aldervale section.

spots.name: Necanicum River Bank (Seaside Residential)
spots.blurb: Residential property visible on river bank in Seaside. Video shows salmon fishing at this specific location in October 2022.
spots.access_note: Residential area with visible house on river bank. Public access status unclear; likely private property.

spots.name: Necanicum River Flounder Hole (Seaside)
spots.blurb: Tidal/estuary section of Necanicum in Seaside where flounder fishing is successful. Video description mentions 'killing it' with new bait, epic catches.
spots.access_note: Estuary/tidal zone access near Seaside. Appears to be accessible public bank area.

spots.name: Social Security Beach (Warrenton Surf Zone)
spots.blurb: Specific named beach access point in Warrenton where salmon surfperch fishing is documented. Video shows successful big salmon catch on the beach.
spots.access_note: Public beach access. Named location 'Social Security Beach' in Warrenton.

spots.name: Coffenbury Lake Access (Warrenton Reservoir)
spots.blurb: Freshwater lake near Warrenton with forested bank access. Video shows welcome/greeting at the location suggesting established public access.
spots.access_note: Public lake access near Warrenton. Trailhead parking available; short walk to water.

spots.name: Nehalem River Mouth to Mountains Survey Section
spots.blurb: BackFishing YouTube series documented exploration of Nehalem River from the sea to the mountains looking for winter steelhead bank access. Multiple pullouts and bank spots identified during this river run.
spots.access_note: Multiple bank access points documented from sea to mountains. Research showed follow-the-river bank access survey.

spots.name: Upper Necanicum Forested Pool (Coastal Range)
spots.blurb: Forested pool with moss-covered banks and dense evergreen canopy visible in Oregon Coast steelhead fishing shorts. Shows pristine remote section upstream from Seaside.
spots.access_note: Remote forested area; likely requires hiking or logging road pullout access. Estimated from aerial positioning of evergreen forest and river bend.

spots.name: Klaskanine Spey Casting Pool
spots.blurb: Deep, wide pool suitable for spey casting documented in winter steelhead video. Shows longer holding water typical of North Fork Klaskanine upper sections.
spots.access_note: Appears to be remote forest access, possibly via logging road. Estimated from coordinates of visible terrain features.

spots.name: Lewis and Clark River Lower Columbia (Sturgeon/Salmon)
spots.water_body: Lewis and Clark River / lower Columbia confluence
spots.blurb: Lower river section where catch-and-release sturgeon fishing is documented. Lewis and Clark Guide Service operates in this area. Accessible by boat.
spots.access_note: Boat access via Lewis and Clark Guide Service. Part of lower Columbia system.

spots.name: From the Field - Lewis and Clark River (Freshwater Trust Project)
spots.blurb: Re-vegetation project area documented by The Freshwater Trust. Shows riparian restoration efforts and fish habitat work on Lewis and Clark River.
spots.access_note: Public access for monitoring/educational purposes as part of Freshwater Trust restoration project.

spots.name: Flyfishing Pool - Coastal Range Forest
spots.water_body: Necanicum River tributary or upper tributary
spots.blurb: Small to medium pool in dense coastal evergreen forest with angler shown flyfishing for steelhead. Deep green water and bank-accessible holding water.
spots.access_note: Remote forested location. Likely requires hiking or logging road access from Highway 26 or 30.

spots.name: Righteous River - Coastal Waterfall Section
spots.blurb: Dramatic waterfall and pool system shown in Righteous River Fishing in Oregon YouTube shorts. Beautiful forested setting with cascade access.
spots.access_note: Remote location; likely trailhead or logging road access. Estimated from visible cascade terrain.

_meta.notes: All spots in this pass are single-source or minimal-mention finds from YouTube videos, shorts, and fishing channels. Many represent forested/remote locations visible in video backgrounds. Access varies from public beach to private land requiring permission. Several are guide-service locations. Coordinates estimated from satellite imagery and visible terrain features in videos.
